player_0.content: New plan: I failed because I misidentified the sarcasm in the final question by focusing on the "dear friend" address rather than the factual absurdity of the object. In option (A), "elephants" are genuinely endangered, making the statement "glad to feed the elephants, that woefully endangered species" a literal, positive sentiment. In option (B), "trolls" are internet users and are not biologically endangered; claiming they are a "woefully endangered species" is a factual error used to mock the listener or the situation, which fits the definition of sarcasm (saying the opposite of what is meant or using absurdity to criticize). My strategy should be to verify the factual truth of the noun phrase before assuming the polite address indicates sarcasm. Next time, I will select (B) because the false claim about trolls being endangered is the sarcastic element.
